title: Question types
lede: What the Legacy portal offers, what OME prefers, and the two types worth learning properly.

blocks.caption: Question types and where OME stands on each
rows: Does most of the work. Handles one or several correct answers, with partial credit options.
In the Legacy portal this is Multiple Choice with more than one answer marked correct, not a separate type.
Two options. Discriminates poorly, so use it sparingly.
Spelling is scored. Up to 15 blanks per question, with alternatives separated by a vertical pipe.
Rectangle and polygon variants. The student drops a pin on the image.
Allows partial credit with negative scoring. Does not score sequence.

blocks.title: Not preferable is an OME judgment, not a limitation
blocks.text: Fill in the Blank and Matching both work. OME discourages them because they produce more scoring disputes and more post-exam adjustment than they are worth. If your course has a good reason to use one, raise it before the draft deadline rather than at proofing.

The student taps a region of an image and a pin drops there. This is the best item type JABSOM has for anatomy, neuroanatomy, and clinical skills, or anywhere the answer is a location rather than a word.

items: Pick **rectangle** or **polygon** first. Rectangle is quicker to define. Polygon is worth the effort on irregular structures.
Add the image by dragging it onto the question or selecting the box below the question text. GIF, JPG, JPEG, and PNG all work.
Drag to outline the correct region. To move a hot spot later, press and hold, then drag it.
Students can pinch to zoom on the iPad, so small structures stay answerable.

blocks.alt: Photograph of an iPad in Examplify preview mode showing a Hot Spot question reading 'Where is the brain?' above a greyscale MRI image. A blue teardrop pin has been dropped near the top of the image. Instructional text explains that the student selects an answer by clicking the desired location on the image, can move the pin by clicking another location, and can remove it by clicking it once. Zoom and reset controls run down the left side.
blocks.caption: A Hot Spot question in Examplify preview on an OME iPad. The blue pin is what the student places.
blocks.note: The dark rectangle over part of the MRI is in the original source photograph.

blocks.text: The student reads a list of possible answers and drags the correct ones into an answer box. Two things about it catch people out.

blocks.title: Drag and Drop does not score sequence
blocks.text: The order a student drags answers into the box makes no difference to the score. If you need sequence scored, use the Ordering type instead.

blocks.title: Partial credit here subtracts points
blocks.text: With partial credit on, a student gains points for each correct answer dragged in and loses the same amount for each wrong one. The score stops at 0 rather than going negative. Warn them in the stem, for example: answer carefully, because dragging incorrect answers into the box can reduce credit. Without that warning students guess and the item stops behaving predictably.
Keep answer choices short. You can put images inside a choice, but large or multiple images render badly.

blocks.caption: The same Drag and Drop question before and after answering, in Examplify preview on an OME iPad.

items.alt: Photograph of an iPad in Examplify preview mode showing a Drag and Drop question reading 'Select what colors are in classic sun flower? Drag the answers to the section.' The left column, headed Possible Colors, lists five draggable options: Black, Brown, Golden Yellow, Bright Yellow, and Pink. The right column, headed Selected Answers, is empty.
items.label: Before: every choice sits in Possible Colors

items.alt: The same iPad Drag and Drop question after answering. The left Possible Colors column now lists only Black and Brown, while the right Selected Answers column contains Golden Yellow, Bright Yellow, and Pink.
items.label: After: three choices moved to Selected Answers

blocks.text: The Legacy portal also offers Ordering and Matrix question types. Neither is in the OME list above and neither appears in any onboarding document, but Ordering is in the student-facing orientation deck, so students may meet it. Decide whether OME wants to sanction either type for pre-clerkship exams and whether to document them here.
